description: Ω1 law spine: the gate (law.check), consent grants, capability-handle algebra, registry (journal replay + the D-416 vault-journal absorb), per-principal forbidden-action overlay (law.forbidden.set, D-310; vault-durable per D-325 with law.forbidden.reload), shadow amendment, and the principal describe read (law.describe, D-353). D-416 (S3, the evidence-store fold): law's narrative journal rows ride vault ns law (id family journal:<boot>-<seq>) wherever port:vault.append@1 is granted — the legacy host sidecar port stays the write path without it (the transition discipline) — and law.audit.drain@1 persists the kernel's signed audit chain into vault ns audit (the persistence point). Replaces the Ω0 law-stub via recipe re-compile + atomic pin swap (D-213).

capabilities.justification: law.check journals every gate decision: with vault caps the narrative row rides vault ns law (the D-416 fold), without them the host law-journal sidecar (host.journal.append — the transition path); law.tokens.revoke delegates plugin token revocation to the host generation bump (host.tokens.revoke). D-325: law.forbidden.set journals the forbidden overlay to vault ns law and reloads it at boot (vault.append/query/get) — granted per-composition by the user-signed Recipe (agent.json), never by this manifest; compositions without the vault grant stay memory-only. D-416 (S3): law.audit.drain@1 exports the kernel audit chain through host.kernel.lens and persists it whole into vault ns audit — the same per-composition grant shape: the cap is requested here, granted only where a signed recipe says so.
